summary: In this special second anniversary episode of the Lord of Spirits podcast, Fathers Andrew Stephen Damick and Stephen DeYoung host a live Q&A session, taking calls from listeners on a variety of theological and practical topics. The episode begins with a humorous call about catching leprechauns, which leads to a discussion of fairy folklore and its connections to spiritual realities. Subsequent calls address the possibility of angels or saints falling again, the branch theory of the church in relation to ancient Israel, the nature of identity and relics, the role of doctrine in the church, and the relationship between idolatry and sexual immorality. The fathers also field questions about the 'Son of Man' title, the canon of Scripture, church architecture, the Most High God, and evangelism. Throughout, they emphasize the importance of understanding spiritual realities, the dangers of materialism and relativism, and the need for a holistic approach to faith that integrates doctrine, practice, and community.

concepts.title: Branch Theory of the Church
concepts.summary: The idea that different Christian denominations are branches of the same Church, which the fathers reject, arguing that schism is a tragedy and that doctrine matters.

concepts.title: Identity as Action
concepts.summary: The concept that identity is not just about essence but also about relationships and activities, as illustrated by the example of a relic of the True Cross.

concepts.title: Natural Will and Gnomic Will
concepts.summary: Distinction between the natural will that impels toward the good and the gnomic will that emerges after the fall as a faculty of indecision.

concepts.title: Angelic and Human Falls
concepts.summary: Discussion on whether angels or saints can fall again, concluding that after reaching maturity in Christ, further falls are not possible.

concepts.title: Most High God
concepts.summary: The title 'Most High God' is used by various religions, but it does not imply they worship the same being; it is a title that belongs to the true God.

concepts.title: Beauty First Approach
concepts.summary: The idea that changing culture and hearts requires a focus on beauty and truth, not just legislation or protest, especially regarding abortion.

concepts.title: Doctrine and Praxis
concepts.summary: The relationship between doctrine and practice: doctrine emerges from practice and serves to protect and define it, not the other way around.

claims.text: Once angels and humans are perfected in Christ, they are preserved by grace and cannot fall again.
Schism is always a tragedy that needs to be healed, not accepted as normal or used to define who is in and out of the Church.
Identity is not just about essence but also about relationships and activities; a phony relic can function as the True Cross for those who venerate it in faith.
Adam was in a state of innocence, not perfection, and was mutable, which is why he could fall.
Doctrine matters because it affects what we do; we are judged by our works, not by our correct opinions.
Evangelism must be contextual, focusing on who Jesus is, what He accomplished, and what He expects, rather than just being right.
To truly address abortion, we need systemic cultural changes that value children and families, not just legislation or charity.

scriptural_links.summary: Used to explain the grafting of Gentiles into Israel, reconstituting the ten northern tribes.

Quoted at the end of the episode about the voice of many angels around the throne.

glossary.definition: The second movement of the will that emerges after the fall, characterized by indecision and the need to choose between alternatives.
The process of becoming like God through participation in His energies, often described as deification.
A person who, without explicit Christian faith, seeks to worship the true God and is accepted by Him, as illustrated by Cornelius.
Florovsky's distinction: dogma is non-negotiable core beliefs, doctrine is the teaching of dogma, and theology is reflection and application.
